statement: Autopsy-acquired cardiac allografts were used to examine biopsy grading reliability as a function of the morphological diagnostic criterion and the number of fragments.
supports: A direct rejection-specific precedent for studying small-biopsy sampling using larger autopsy material.
does_not_establish: Abstract-only review; no numerical error rate indexed. Historical criteria are not modern 0R-3R labels. Not a biopsy/autopsy AI training experiment.
method_or_result: Comparison of inflammation-pattern and myocyte-necrosis criteria with attention to biopsy fragment number.

statement: In hearts known to have lymphocytic myocarditis at autopsy, biopsy-sized specimens frequently missed diagnostic inflammation, illustrating spatial sampling error even when multiple specimens were examined.
supports: A rationale for distinguishing disease in the whole heart from visible diagnostic lesions in a sampled biopsy or cropped region.
does_not_establish: Myocarditis is not transplant rejection; no modern ACR sensitivity estimate follows. Postmortem simulated biopsies are not independent clinical biopsy validation and a whole-heart diagnosis cannot label every crop as positive.
method_or_result: Comparison of ten biopsy-sized samples per ventricle with larger ventricular myocardial slices using Dallas criteria.

statement: Biopsy C4d immunoreactivity was associated with subsequent cardiac allograft vasculopathy and death; autopsy findings were used in the outcome assessment of a deceased subset.
supports: A heart-transplant precedent for linking biopsy marker information to later autopsy pathology rather than treating the two specimen types as interchangeable.
does_not_establish: Association is not causation. C4d/CAV, AMR and ACR are distinct targets; no biopsy/autopsy AI benefit or retrospective correction of an earlier ACR label is established. Abstract-only review; no current guideline recommendation is inferred.
method_or_result: Correlation of biopsy C4d immunoreactivity with cardiac dysfunction, HLA status, CAV and death.

statement: The study compared earlier right-ventricular biopsy fibrosis with later whole-heart fibrosis in the same patients, combining 52 explant and 18 autopsy cases; biopsy-to-excision time was explicitly considered.
supports: A concrete matched-patient design for connecting small biopsies to larger cardiac specimens while retaining chronology.
does_not_establish: DCM native-heart fibrosis is not rejection in a transplanted heart. Explant and autopsy are different specimen origins. Not AI transfer, not proof of stable pathology across the intervening years, and no rejection-performance benefit follows.
method_or_result: Image-based fibrosis-area measurement in biopsy and larger-heart sections, with analysis accounting for biopsy-to-excision interval.

statement: SongCi learned representations from postmortem WSI and text; the main article also reports transfer evaluation on three clinical WSI datasets and five patch datasets, beyond forensic tasks.
supports: A more direct precedent that autopsy-derived representations can be evaluated on clinical pathology tasks, motivating a controlled source-to-target comparison.
does_not_establish: Clinical transfer benchmarks concern tumor/clinical pathology, not heart-transplant biopsy rejection. Main-text report only: Supplementary Tables 9-10, overlap controls, tuning details and quantitative transfer results were not audited. Does not show benefit over current UNI v2 or justify training on held-out SMC patients.
method_or_result: Prototypical and cross-modal contrastive representation learning; forensic validation and reported clinical-pathology transfer benchmarks.

statement: Despite biopsy-oriented framing, the reported experiment used 60 microscopic images from six autopsy subjects; it did not test transfer to living-patient endomyocardial biopsies.
supports: A small-model cardiac autopsy example whose actual specimen origin and number of independent patients must remain explicit.
does_not_establish: Six patients and microscopic fields are not an independent clinical biopsy cohort. No biopsy/autopsy joint-learning benefit, rejection discrimination, WSI generalization, or fully audited patient-separated validation is established. High reported image-level performance must not be transferred to SMC.
method_or_result: Texture features, feature selection/dimensional compression, and classical classifiers including linear SVM.
